title: Planning accessibility from the start
when: Any job with a user interface, so that accessibility is built into tasks instead of patched after QA.
prompt:
Goal: Accessibility requirements written into each task detail and the criteria, so the first draft already meets WCAG basics.
Steps:
1. List interactive parts: forms, menus, dialogs, tabs, custom controls, games.
2. For each, write the requirement in the owner task: native element first (button, label, details), keyboard path, visible focus, name for screen readers.
3. Put contrast and sizes into the designer task: 4.5 to 1 for text, 44 px touch targets, focus ring visible, reduced motion respected.
4. Put content rules into the writer task: alt text per image, link text that makes sense alone, clear error messages.
5. Add criteria QA can test: everything works with Tab and Enter, labels on every field, one h1 per page.
6. Attach the matching checks (labels, focus, contrast, aria-live) to the QA task.
Quality bar:
- Every interactive part has a keyboard path in its task.
- Native elements are preferred over ARIA.
- Criteria include accessibility lines.
Pitfalls:
- A single "make it accessible" task at the end.
- Divs used as buttons.
- ARIA added where a native element would do.
Verify:
- [ ] Interactive parts listed.
- [ ] Each owner task has its requirement.
- [ ] Designer and writer tasks include their rules.
- [ ] QA criteria test keyboard and labels.
Output: Task details and acceptance criteria with accessibility lines; no separate accessibility task.

examples.output: dev: fieldset per step, labels, focus moves to step heading; designer: focus ring, contrast; qa: Tab through all steps
